metadata.blurb: Zeus is a truly seedless and decentralized self-custodial Ethereum wallet.

ref.explanation: Zeus derives a Hierarchical Deterministic Wallet from a username and password using the BIP32 standard. Users can also import wallets using either a 12-24 word phrase or a private key.
Zeus's send UI validates recipients by parsing the input as an Ethereum address with `Address::from_str`; repository search found no ENS, namehash, resolver, or Universal Resolver implementation.
The Zeus send flow checks recipient input with `Address::from_str`, so non-address names such as ENS names are rejected as invalid recipients rather than resolved.
Zeus has a built-in interface which uses the Across protocol to bridge ETH between chains.
Zeus uses public RPC endpoints by default but allows users to provide custom endpoints and disable or delete what they don't want.
Users can use their own RPC endpoints.
Zeus is licensed under the MIT license.
The Zeus README states that Zeus has no telemetry and does not communicate with any third-party server; activity stays local on the user computer.
The Zeus README states that Zeus has no telemetry and does not communicate with any third-party server; activity stays local on the user computer.
Zeus exposes the address of the active account only.
Zeus uses a username and password to derive the master HD wallet. Recovery is only possible by using the same username and password.
Zeus uses a username and password to derive the master HD wallet; recovery is only possible by using the same username and password.

Zeus documents wallet management through username/password-derived wallets plus seed-phrase and private-key imports; no public hardware-wallet pairing or signing support is documented in the README, and repository search found no Ledger, Trezor, or hardware-wallet integration.
Keys are generated fully on the user device using BIP32 derivation from a seed derived via Argon2Id from username and password.

Zeus currently does not have a scam alert mechanism, It simply shows with which contract you are interacting with. If it is a known contract a hyperlink with the contracts name is shown otherwise a truncated version of the contract address is shown (hyperlink). The user can also see all the decoded events to inspect the transaction.
ref.label: Contract interaction is shown in the transaction details
Before every transaction the user must confirm the action.

ref.explanation: Zeus performs local EVM simulations to verify and display exact transaction outcomes, including decoding of common events like erc20 transfers, swaps, approvals etc...
Zeus performs local EVM simulations with revm before transaction submission and decodes transfers, token approvals, permits, bridge deposits, Uniswap swaps, and failed outcomes from logs.
The Zeus README says the wallet does not automatically index data like token approvals, because it works from Ethereum RPC APIs rather than third-party indexing services.
Zeus submits transactions via RPC endpoints.
Users can provide their own RPC endpoint to a self-hosted node.
Zeus submits L2 transactions via RPC endpoints.

Zeus publishes locked Rust dependencies in Cargo.lock and a production profile in Cargo.toml, but the public repository does not document deterministic rebuild-and-compare verification for matching published desktop release artifacts.

The Zeus Cargo.lock file pins registry package versions and checksums for dependency resolution; this supports repeatable dependency selection but is not a published reproducible-build verification workflow for release binaries.

Zeus is a self-custodial desktop Ethereum wallet whose README lists its features (send, bridge, swap, portfolio, simulations) with no fiat on-ramp, and explicitly states it does not rely on any third-party service.
The README documents no crypto-to-fiat off-ramp; only crypto operations like swaps and bridging are supported, and a GitHub code search found zero references to any ramp providers.
Zeus has no fiat ramp, so bank transfer (ACH/SEPA/wire) is not available as a payment method.
Zeus has no fiat ramp at all, so card payments are not available as a purchase method.
